{'en': 'Machine reading using differentiable reasoning models has recently shown remarkable progress. In this context, End-to-End trainable Memory Networks (MemN2N) have demonstrated promising performance on simple natural language based reasoning tasks such as factual reasoning and basic deduction. However, other tasks, namely multi-fact question-answering, positional reasoning or dialog related tasks, remain challenging particularly due to the necessity of more complex interactions between the memory and controller modules composing this family of models. In this paper, we introduce a novel end-to-end memory access regulation mechanism inspired by the current progress on the connection short-cutting principle in the field of computer vision. Concretely, we develop a Gated End-to-End trainable Memory Network architecture (GMemN2N). From the machine learning perspective, this new capability is learned in an end-to-end fashion without the use of any additional supervision signal which is, as far as our knowledge goes, the first of its kind. Our experiments show significant improvements on the most challenging tasks in the 20 bAbI dataset, without the use of any domain knowledge. Then, we show improvements on the Dialog bAbI tasks including the real human-bot conversion-based Dialog State Tracking Challenge (DSTC-2) dataset. {'en': 'Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) process input text sequentially and model the conditional transition between word tokens. In this paper, we introduce a robust syntactic parsing-independent tree structured model, Neural Tree Indexers (NTI) that provides a middle ground between the sequential RNNs and the syntactic treebased recursive models. {'en': 'Our goal is to combine the rich multi-step inference of symbolic logical reasoning with the generalization capabilities of neural networks. We are particularly interested in complex reasoning about entities and relations in text and large-scale knowledge bases (KBs). Neelakantan et al. (2015) use RNNs to compose the distributed semantics of multi-hop paths in KBs ; however for multiple reasons, the approach lacks accuracy and practicality. This paper proposes three significant modeling advances : (1) we learn to jointly reason about relations, entities, and entity-types ; (2) we use neural attention modeling to incorporate multiple paths ; (3) we learn to share strength in a single RNN that represents logical composition across all relations. {'en': 'Language contains information about the author’s demographic attributes as well as their mental state, and has been successfully leveraged in NLP to predict either one alone. However, demographic attributes and mental states also interact with each other, and we are the first to demonstrate how to use them jointly to improve the prediction of mental health conditions across the board. {'en': 'Sentiment Analysis is a broad task that involves the analysis of various aspect of the natural language text. However, most of the approaches in the state of the art usually investigate independently each aspect, i.e. Subjectivity Classification, Sentiment Polarity Classification, Emotion Recognition, Irony Detection. In this paper we present a Multi-View Sentiment Corpus (MVSC), which comprises 3000 English microblog posts related the movie domain. {'en': 'In an end-to-end dialog system, the aim of dialog state tracking is to accurately estimate a compact representation of the current dialog status from a sequence of noisy observations produced by the speech recognition and the natural language understanding modules. This paper introduces a novel method of dialog state tracking based on the general paradigm of machine reading and proposes to solve it using an End-to-End Memory Network, MemN2N, a memory-enhanced neural network architecture. We evaluate the proposed approach on the second Dialog State Tracking Challenge (DSTC-2) dataset. The corpus has been converted for the occasion in order to frame the hidden state variable inference as a question-answering task based on a sequence of utterances extracted from a dialog. We show that the proposed tracker gives encouraging results. Then, we propose to extend the DSTC-2 dataset with specific reasoning capabilities requirement like counting, list maintenance, yes-no question answering and indefinite knowledge management. Finally, we present encouraging results using our proposed MemN2N based tracking model.', 'fr': "Dans un système de dialogue de bout en bout, le but du suivi d'état de dialogue est d'estimer avec précision une représentation compacte de l'état actuel du dialogue à partir d'une séquence d'observations bruyantes produites par les modules de reconnaissance vocale et de compréhension du langage naturel. Cet article présente une nouvelle méthode de suivi d'état de dialogue basée sur le paradigme général de la lecture automatique et propose de la résoudre à l'aide d'un réseau de mémoire de bout en bout, MEMN2n, une architecture de réseau neuronal améliorée en mémoire. Nous évaluons l'approche proposée sur le deuxième jeu de données Dialog State Tracking Challenge (DSTC-2). {'en': 'Automated discourse analysis tools based on Natural Language Processing (NLP) aiming at the diagnosis of language-impairing dementias generally extract several textual metrics of narrative transcripts. However, the absence of sentence boundary segmentation in the transcripts prevents the direct application of NLP methods which rely on these marks in order to function properly, such as taggers and parsers. We present the first steps taken towards automatic neuropsychological evaluation based on narrative discourse analysis, presenting a new automatic sentence segmentation method for impaired speech. Our model uses recurrent convolutional neural networks with prosodic, Part of Speech (PoS) features, and word embeddings. It was evaluated intrinsically on impaired, spontaneous speech as well as normal, prepared speech and presents better results for healthy elderly (CTL) (F1 = 0.74) and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) patients (F1 = 0.70) than the Conditional Random Fields method (F1 = 0.55 and 0.53, respectively) used in the same context of our study. Vores model bruger tilbagevendende konvulutionelle neurale netværk med prosodiske, Part of Speech (PoS) funktioner og ordindlejringer. {'en': 'Teaching machines to accomplish tasks by conversing naturally with humans is challenging. Currently, developing task-oriented dialogue systems requires creating multiple components and typically this involves either a large amount of handcrafting, or acquiring costly labelled datasets to solve a statistical learning problem for each component. {'en': 'In this paper we tackle a unique and important problem of extracting a structured order from the conversation a customer has with an order taker at a restaurant. This is motivated by an actual system under development to assist in the order taking process. We develop a sequence-to-sequence model that is able to map from unstructured conversational input to the structured form that is conveyed to the kitchen and appears on the customer receipt. {'en': 'This paper presents a method for applying automatically acquired knowledge to semantic role labeling (SRL). We use a large amount of automatically extracted knowledge to improve the performance of SRL. We present two varieties of knowledge, which we call surface case frames and deep case frames. Although the surface case frames are compiled from syntactic parses and can be used as rich syntactic knowledge, they have limited capability for resolving semantic ambiguity. In this paper, we present methods for learning multi-level representations of entities on three complementary levels : character (character patterns in entity names extracted, e.g., by neural networks), word (embeddings of words in entity names) and entity (entity embeddings). The problem is very challenging and has been divided into sub-problems such as mention and named entity recognition, entity linking and relation extraction. However, combining these components has shown to be under-constrained and often produces KBs with supersize entities and common-sense errors in relations (a person has multiple birthdates). The errors are difficult to resolve solely with IE tools but become obvious with world knowledge at the corpus level. {'en': 'Universal schema predicts the types of entities and relations in a knowledge base (KB) by jointly embedding the union of all available schema typesnot only types from multiple structured databases (such as Freebase or Wikipedia infoboxes), but also types expressed as textual patterns from raw text. This prediction is typically modeled as a matrix completion problem, with one type per column, and either one or two entities per row (in the case of entity types or binary relation types, respectively). Factorizing this sparsely observed matrix yields a learned vector embedding for each row and each column. In this paper we explore the problem of making predictions for entities or entity-pairs unseen at training time (and hence without a pre-learned row embedding). We propose an approach having no per-row parameters at all ; rather we produce a row vector on the fly using a learned aggregation function of the vectors of the observed columns for that row. We experiment with various aggregation functions, including neural network attention models. Our approach can be understood as a natural language database, in that questions about KB entities are answered by attending to textual or database evidence. In experiments predicting both relations and entity types, we demonstrate that despite having an order of magnitude fewer parameters than traditional universal schema, we can match the accuracy of the traditional model, and more importantly, we can now make predictions about unseen rows with nearly the same accuracy as rows available at training time.', 'ar': 'يتنبأ المخطط العام بأنواع الكيانات والعلاقات في قاعدة المعرفة (KB) من خلال التضمين المشترك لجميع أنواع المخططات المتاحة - ليس فقط الأنواع من قواعد البيانات المنظمة المتعددة (مثل Freebase أو Wikipedia Infoboxes) ، ولكن أيضًا الأنواع المعبر عنها كنماذج نصية من النص الخام. عادة ما يتم نمذجة هذا التوقع كمشكلة إكمال مصفوفة ، بنوع واحد لكل عمود ، وكيان واحد أو كيانين لكل صف (في حالة أنواع الكيانات أو أنواع العلاقات الثنائية ، على التوالي). يؤدي تحليل هذه المصفوفة التي تمت ملاحظتها بشكل ضئيل إلى تضمين متجه متعلم لكل صف وكل عمود. في هذه الورقة ، نستكشف مشكلة عمل التنبؤات للكيانات أو أزواج الكيانات غير المرئية في وقت التدريب (وبالتالي بدون تضمين صف تم تعلمه مسبقًا). نقترح نهجًا لا يحتوي على معلمات لكل صف على الإطلاق ؛ بدلاً من ذلك ، ننتج متجهًا للصف سريعًا باستخدام دالة تجميع متعلمة لمتجهات الأعمدة المرصودة لهذا الصف. نقوم بتجربة وظائف التجميع المختلفة ، بما في ذلك نماذج انتباه الشبكة العصبية. يمكن فهم نهجنا على أنه قاعدة بيانات للغة الطبيعية ، حيث تتم الإجابة على الأسئلة المتعلقة بكيانات قاعدة البيانات من خلال حضور أدلة نصية أو أدلة قواعد البيانات. في التجارب التي تتنبأ بكل من العلاقات وأنواع الكيانات ، أوضحنا أنه على الرغم من وجود عدد أقل من المعلمات بترتيب من حيث الحجم مقارنة بالمخطط العام التقليدي ، يمكننا مطابقة دقة النموذج التقليدي ، والأهم من ذلك ، يمكننا الآن عمل تنبؤات حول ما هو غير مرئي\nصفوف بنفس دقة الصفوف المتوفرة في وقت التدريب تقريبًا.', 'es': 'El esquema universal predice los tipos de entidades y relaciones en una base de conocimientos (KB) mediante la incorporación conjunta de la unión de todos los tipos de esquemas disponibles, no solo los tipos de múltiples bases de datos estructuradas (como las infoboxes de Freebase o Wikipedia), sino también los tipos expresados como patrones textuales de texto sin formato. Esta predicción generalmente se modela como un problema de finalización de matrices, con un tipo por columna y una o dos entidades por fila (en el caso de tipos de entidad o tipos de relación binaria, respectivamente). La factorización de esta matriz escasamente observada produce un vector aprendido que se incrusta para cada fila y cada columna. En este artículo exploramos el problema de hacer predicciones para entidades o pares de entidades que no se ven en el momento del entrenamiento (y, por lo tanto, sin una incrustación de filas previamente aprendida). Proponemos un enfoque que no tiene ningún parámetro por fila; más bien, producimos un vector de fila sobre la marcha utilizando una función de agregación aprendida de los vectores de las columnas observadas para esa fila. Traditional natural language generation methods rely extensively on hand-crafted rules and predefined templates. This paper presents an attention-enhanced attribute-to-sequence model to generate product reviews for given attribute information, such as user, product, and rating. The attribute encoder learns to represent input attributes as vectors. Then, the sequence decoder generates reviews by conditioning its output on these vectors. We also introduce an attention mechanism to jointly generate reviews and align words with input attributes. The proposed model is trained end-to-end to maximize the likelihood of target product reviews given the attributes. We build a publicly available dataset for the review generation task by leveraging the Amazon book reviews and their metadata. {'en': 'We use the noisy-channel theory of human sentence comprehension to develop an incremental processing cost model that unifies and extends key features of expectation-based and memory-based models. In this model, which we call noisy-context surprisal, the processing cost of a word is the surprisal of the word given a noisy representation of the preceding context. We show that this model accounts for an outstanding puzzle in sentence comprehension, language-dependent structural forgetting effects (Gibson and Thomas, 1999 ; Vasishth et al., 2010 ; Frank et al., 2016), which are previously not well modeled by either expectation-based or memory-based approaches. Additionally, we show that this model derives and generalizes locality effects (Gibson, 1998 ; Demberg and Keller, 2008), a signature prediction of memory-based models. {'en': 'This work studies comparatively two typical sentence matching tasks : textual entailment (TE) and answer selection (AS), observing that weaker phrase alignments are more critical in TE, while stronger phrase alignments deserve more attention in AS. The key to reach this observation lies in phrase detection, phrase representation, phrase alignment, and more importantly how to connect those aligned phrases of different matching degrees with the final classifier. Prior work (i) has limitations in phrase generation and representation, or (ii) conducts alignment at word and phrase levels by handcrafted features or (iii) utilizes a single framework of alignment without considering the characteristics of specific tasks, which limits the framework’s effectiveness across tasks. We propose an architecture based on Gated Recurrent Unit that supports (i) representation learning of phrases of arbitrary granularity and (ii) task-specific attentive pooling of phrase alignments between two sentences. {'en': 'To extract structured representations of newsworthy events from Twitter, unsupervised models typically assume that tweets involving the same named entities and expressed using similar words are likely to belong to the same event. Hence, they group tweets into clusters based on the co-occurrence patterns of named entities and topical keywords. However, there are two main limitations. First, they require the number of events to be known beforehand, which is not realistic in practical applications. {'en': 'We introduce automatic verification as a post-processing step for entity linking (EL). The proposed method trusts EL system results collectively, by assuming entity mentions are mostly linked correctly, in order to create a semantic profile of the given text using geospatial and temporal information, as well as fine-grained entity types. This profile is then used to automatically verify each linked mention individually, i.e., to predict whether it has been linked correctly or not. Verification allows leveraging a rich set of global and pairwise features that would be prohibitively expensive for EL systems employing global inference. Evaluation shows consistent improvements across datasets and systems. In particular, when applied to state-of-the-art systems, our method yields an absolute improvement in linking performance of up to 1.7 F1 on AIDA / CoNLL’03 and up to 2.4 F1 on the English TAC KBP 2015 TEDL dataset.', 'ar': "نقدم التحقق التلقائي كخطوة ما بعد المعالجة لربط الكيان (EL). تثق الطريقة المقترحة في نتائج نظام EL بشكل جماعي ، بافتراض ارتباط إشارات الكيانات في الغالب بشكل صحيح ، من أجل إنشاء ملف تعريف دلالي للنص المحدد باستخدام المعلومات الجغرافية المكانية والزمانية ، بالإضافة إلى أنواع الكيانات الدقيقة. ثم يتم استخدام ملف التعريف هذا للتحقق تلقائيًا من كل إشارة مرتبطة بشكل فردي ، أي للتنبؤ بما إذا كان قد تم ربطها بشكل صحيح أم لا. يسمح التحقق بالاستفادة من مجموعة غنية من الميزات العالمية والزوجية التي قد تكون باهظة التكلفة لأنظمة EL التي تستخدم الاستدلال العالمي. يُظهر التقييم تحسينات متسقة عبر مجموعات البيانات والأنظمة. على وجه الخصوص ، عند تطبيقها على أحدث الأنظمة ، تؤدي طريقتنا إلى تحسين مطلق في ربط أداء يصل إلى 1.7 F1 على AIDA / CoNLL'03 وحتى 2.4 F1 على مجموعة بيانات TEDL الإنجليزية TAC KBP 2015.", 'fr': "Nous introduisons la vérification automatique en tant qu'étape de post-traitement pour la liaison d'entités (EL). {'en': 'Enabling machines to read and comprehend unstructured text remains an unfulfilled goal for NLP research. Recent research efforts on the machine comprehension task have managed to achieve close to ideal performance on simulated data. However, achieving similar levels of performance on small real world datasets has proved difficult ; major challenges stem from the large vocabulary size, complex grammar, and, the frequent ambiguities in linguistic structure. On the other hand, the requirement of human generated annotations for training, in order to ensure a sufficiently diverse set of questions is prohibitively expensive. Motivated by these practical issues, we propose a novel curriculum inspired training procedure for Memory Networks to improve the performance for machine comprehension with relatively small volumes of training data. Additionally, we explore various training regimes for Memory Networks to allow knowledge transfer from a closely related domain having larger volumes of labelled data. We also suggest the use of a loss function to incorporate the asymmetric nature of knowledge transfer. {'en': 'In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised algorithm for word sense disambiguation (WSD) at the document level. Our algorithm is inspired by a widely-used approach in the field of genetics for whole genome sequencing, known as the Shotgun sequencing technique. The proposed WSD algorithm is based on three main steps. First, a brute-force WSD algorithm is applied to short context windows (up to 10 words) selected from the document in order to generate a short list of likely sense configurations for each window. In the second step, these local sense configurations are assembled into longer composite configurations based on suffix and prefix matching. The resulted configurations are ranked by their length, and the sense of each word is chosen based on a voting scheme that considers only the top k configurations in which the word appears. We compare our algorithm with other state-of-the-art unsupervised WSD algorithms and demonstrate better performance, sometimes by a very large margin. We also show that our algorithm can yield better performance than the Most Common Sense (MCS) baseline on one data set. Moreover, our algorithm has a very small number of parameters, is robust to parameter tuning, and, unlike other bio-inspired methods, it gives a deterministic solution (it does not involve random choices).', 'pt': 'Neste artigo, apresentamos um novo algoritmo não supervisionado para desambiguação de sentido de palavra (WSD) no nível do documento. Nosso algoritmo é inspirado em uma abordagem amplamente utilizada no campo da genética para sequenciamento de genoma inteiro, conhecida como técnica de sequenciamento Shotgun. O algoritmo WSD proposto é baseado em três etapas principais. Primeiro, um algoritmo WSD de força bruta é aplicado a janelas de contexto curtas (até 10 palavras) selecionadas do documento para gerar uma pequena lista de configurações de sentido prováveis para cada janela. Na segunda etapa, essas configurações de sentido local são montadas em configurações compostas mais longas com base na correspondência de sufixo e prefixo. As configurações resultantes são classificadas por seu comprimento, e o sentido de cada palavra é escolhido com base em um esquema de votação que considera apenas as k principais configurações em que a palavra aparece. {'en': 'Traditional learning-based approaches to sentiment analysis of written text use the concept of bag-of-words or bag-of-n-grams, where a document is viewed as a set of terms or short combinations of terms disregarding grammar rules or word order. Novel approaches de-emphasize this concept and view the problem as a sequence classification problem. In this context, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have achieved significant success. The idea is to use RNNs as discriminative binary classifiers to predict a positive or negative sentiment label at every word position then perform a type of pooling to get a sentence-level polarity. Here, we investigate a novel generative approach in which a separate probability distribution is estimated for every sentiment using language models (LMs) based on long short-term memory (LSTM) RNNs. We introduce a novel type of LM using a modified version of bidirectional LSTM (BLSTM) called contextual BLSTM (cBLSTM), where the probability of a word is estimated based on its full left and right contexts. Our approach is compared with a BLSTM binary classifier. Significant improvements are observed in classifying the IMDB movie review dataset. {'en': 'Weighted finite automata and transducers (including hidden Markov models and conditional random fields) are widely used in natural language processing (NLP) to perform tasks such as morphological analysis, part-of-speech tagging, chunking, named entity recognition, speech recognition, and others. Parallelizing finite state algorithms on graphics processing units (GPUs) would benefit many areas of NLP. Although researchers have implemented GPU versions of basic graph algorithms, no work, to our knowledge, has been done on GPU algorithms for weighted finite automata. {'en': 'Text mining has drawn significant attention in recent past due to the rapid growth in biomedical and clinical records. Entity extraction is one of the fundamental components for biomedical text mining. In this paper, we propose a novel approach of feature selection for entity extraction that exploits the concept of deep learning and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The system utilizes word embedding features along with several other features extracted by studying the properties of the datasets. We obtain an interesting observation that compact word embedding features as determined by PSO are more effective compared to the entire word embedding feature set for entity extraction. The proposed system is evaluated on three benchmark biomedical datasets such as GENIA, GENETAG, and AiMed. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evident with significant performance gains over the baseline models as well as the other existing systems. We observe improvements of 7.86 %, 5.27 % and 7.25 % F-measure points over the baseline models for GENIA, GENETAG, and AiMed dataset respectively.', 'pt': 'A mineração de texto atraiu atenção significativa no passado recente devido ao rápido crescimento em registros biomédicos e clínicos. {'en': 'Most current approaches in phylogenetic linguistics require as input multilingual word lists partitioned into sets of etymologically related words (cognates). Cognate identification is so far done manually by experts, which is time consuming and as of yet only available for a small number of well-studied language families. Automatizing this step will greatly expand the empirical scope of phylogenetic methods in linguistics, as raw wordlists (in phonetic transcription) are much easier to obtain than wordlists in which cognate words have been fully identified and annotated, even for under-studied languages. A couple of different methods have been proposed in the past, but they are either disappointing regarding their performance or not applicable to larger datasets. Here we present a new approach that uses support vector machines to unify different state-of-the-art methods for phonetic alignment and cognate detection within a single framework. Para melhorar a capacidade de análise de UD, propomos um algoritmo de conversão de vai-e-vem, no qual pré-processamos o banco de árvores de treinamento para aumentar a capacidade de análise e reconvertemos as saídas do analisador para seguir o esquema de UD como um pós-processamento. {'en': 'Several corpora have been annotated with negation scopethe set of words whose meaning is negated by a cue like the word notleading to the development of classifiers that detect negation scope with high accuracy. We show that for nearly all of these corpora, this high accuracy can be attributed to a single fact : they frequently annotate negation scope as a single span of text delimited by punctuation. For negation scopes not of this form, detection accuracy is low and under-sampling the easy training examples does not substantially improve accuracy. We demonstrate that this is partly an artifact of annotation guidelines, and we argue that future negation scope annotation efforts should focus on these more difficult cases.', 'ar': 'تم شرح العديد من المجموعات بنطاق النفي - مجموعة الكلمات التي يتم إنكار معناها من خلال إشارة مثل كلمة "لا" - مما يؤدي إلى تطوير المصنفات التي تكتشف نطاق النفي بدقة عالية. نوضح أنه بالنسبة لجميع هذه المجموعات تقريبًا ، يمكن أن تُعزى هذه الدقة العالية إلى حقيقة واحدة: فهي تعلق في كثير من الأحيان على نطاق الرفض باعتباره امتدادًا واحدًا للنص محددًا بعلامات الترقيم. بالنسبة إلى نطاقات النفي التي ليست من هذا النموذج ، تكون دقة الكشف منخفضة ولا تؤدي أمثلة التدريب السهلة إلى تحسين الدقة بشكل كبير. نوضح أن هذا جزء من إرشادات التعليقات التوضيحية ، ونجادل بأن جهود التعليقات التوضيحية لنطاق الرفض المستقبلية يجب أن تركز على هذه الحالات الأكثر صعوبة.', 'es': 'Se han anotado varios corpus con alcance de negación, el conjunto de palabras cuyo significado se niega con una señal como la palabra «no», lo que lleva al desarrollo de clasificadores que detectan el alcance de la negación con gran precisión. {'en': 'The Parallel Meaning Bank is a corpus of translations annotated with shared, formal meaning representations comprising over 11 million words divided over four languages (English, German, Italian, and Dutch). Our approach is based on cross-lingual projection : automatically produced (and manually corrected) semantic annotations for English sentences are mapped onto their word-aligned translations, assuming that the translations are meaning-preserving. The semantic annotation consists of five main steps : (i) segmentation of the text in sentences and lexical items ; (ii) syntactic parsing with Combinatory Categorial Grammar ; (iii) universal semantic tagging ; (iv) symbolization ; and (v) compositional semantic analysis based on Discourse Representation Theory. These steps are performed using statistical models trained in a semi-supervised manner. The employed annotation models are all language-neutral. {'en': 'We present a novel scheme to combine neural machine translation (NMT) with traditional statistical machine translation (SMT). Our approach borrows ideas from linearised lattice minimum Bayes-risk decoding for SMT. The NMT score is combined with the Bayes-risk of the translation according the SMT lattice. This makes our approach much more flexible than n-best list or lattice rescoring as the neural decoder is not restricted to the SMT search space. We show an efficient and simple way to integrate risk estimation into the NMT decoder which is suitable for word-level as well as subword-unit-level NMT. We test our method on English-German and Japanese-English and report significant gains over lattice rescoring on several data sets for both single and ensembled NMT. {'en': 'The success of sentence classification often depends on understanding both the syntactic and semantic properties of word-phrases. Recent progress on this task has been based on exploiting the grammatical structure of sentences but often this structure is difficult to parse and noisy. In this paper, we propose a structure-independent ‘Gated Representation Alignment’ (GRA) model that blends a phrase-focused Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach with sequence-oriented Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). Our novel alignment mechanism allows the RNN to selectively include phrase information in a word-by-word sentence representation, and to do this without awareness of the syntactic structure. An empirical evaluation of GRA shows higher prediction accuracy (up to 4.6 %) of fine-grained sentiment ratings, when compared to other structure-independent baselines. We also show comparable results to several structure-dependent methods. {'en': 'In many natural language processing (NLP) tasks, a document is commonly modeled as a bag of words using the term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) vector. One major shortcoming of the frequency-based TF-IDF feature vector is that it ignores word orders that carry syntactic and semantic relationships among the words in a document. This paper proposes a novel distributed vector representation of a document, which will be labeled as DV-LSTM, and is derived from the result of adapting a long short-term memory recurrent neural network language model by the document. DV-LSTM is expected to capture some high-level sequential information in the document, which other current document representations fail to do. It was evaluated in document genre classification in the Brown Corpus and the BNC Baby Corpus. {'en': 'In this paper we study the impact of using images to machine-translate user-generated e-commerce product listings. We study how a multi-modal Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model compares to two text-only approaches : a conventional state-of-the-art attentional NMT and a Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) model. User-generated product listings often do not constitute grammatical or well-formed sentences. More often than not, they consist of the juxtaposition of short phrases or keywords. We train our models end-to-end as well as use text-only and multi-modal NMT models for re-ranking n-best lists generated by an SMT model. We qualitatively evaluate our user-generated training data also analyse how adding synthetic data impacts the results. We evaluate our models quantitatively using BLEU and TER and find that (i) additional synthetic data has a general positive impact on text-only and multi-modal NMT models, and that (ii) using a multi-modal NMT model for re-ranking n-best lists improves TER significantly across different n-best list sizes.n-best lists generated by an SMT model. Naše modely trénujeme end-to-end, stejně jako textové a multimodální NMT modely pro přehodnocení n-best seznamů generovaných SMT modelem. {'en': 'In semantic parsing, natural language questions map to expressions in a meaning representation language (MRL) over some fixed vocabulary of predicates. To do this reliably, one must guarantee that for a wide class of natural language questions (the so called semantically tractable questions), correct interpretations are always in the mapped set of possibilities. In this demonstration, we introduce the system COVER which significantly clarifies, revises and extends the basic notion of semantic tractability. COVER achieves coverage of 89 % while the earlier PRECISE system achieved coverage of 77 % on the well known GeoQuery corpus. Like PRECISE, COVER requires only a simple domain lexicon and integrates off-the-shelf syntactic parsers. Beyond PRECISE, COVER also integrates off-the-shelf theorem provers to provide more accurate results. {'en': 'This paper presents Autobank, a prototype tool for constructing a wide-coverage Minimalist Grammar (MG) (Stabler 1997), and semi-automatically converting the Penn Treebank (PTB) into a deep Minimalist treebank. The front end of the tool is a graphical user interface which facilitates the rapid development of a seed set of MG trees via manual reannotation of PTB preterminals with MG lexical categories. The system then extracts various dependency mappings between the source and target trees, and uses these in concert with a non-statistical MG parser to automatically reannotate the rest of the corpus. Autobank thus enables deep treebank conversions (and subsequent modifications) without the need for complex transduction algorithms accompanied by cascades of ad hoc rules ; instead, the locus of human effort falls directly on the task of grammar construction itself.', 'ar': 'تقدم هذه الورقة Autobank ، أداة نموذجية أولية لبناء قواعد نحوية مبسطة واسعة التغطية (MG) (Stabler 1997) ، وتحويل بن تريبانك (PTB) بشكل شبه تلقائي إلى بنك شجر مبسط عميق. الواجهة الأمامية للأداة عبارة عن واجهة مستخدم رسومية تسهل التطوير السريع لمجموعة البذور من أشجار MG عبر إعادة الملحوظات اليدوية لخطوات PTB المسبقة مع فئات MG المعجمية. يقوم النظام بعد ذلك باستخراج تعيينات التبعية المختلفة بين الأشجار المصدر والهدف ، ويستخدمها بالتنسيق مع محلل MG غير الإحصائي لإعادة عرض بقية المجموعة تلقائيًا. وبالتالي ، يتيح Autobank إجراء عمليات تحويل عميقة لضفاف الأشجار (والتعديلات اللاحقة) دون الحاجة إلى خوارزميات تحويل معقدة مصحوبة بسلسلة من القواعد المخصصة ؛ بدلاً من ذلك ، يقع مركز الجهد البشري مباشرة على مهمة بناء القواعد نفسها.', 'pt': 'Este artigo apresenta o Autobank, uma ferramenta protótipo para construir uma Gramática Minimalista (MG) de ampla cobertura (Stabler 1997), e converter semi-automaticamente o Penn Treebank (PTB) em um treebank minimalista profundo. O front-end da ferramenta é uma interface gráfica de usuário que facilita o desenvolvimento rápido de um conjunto de sementes de árvores MG através da reanotação manual de pré-terminais PTB com categorias lexicais MG. {'en': 'Spelling variation in non-standard language, e.g. computer-mediated communication and historical texts, is usually treated as a deviation from a standard spelling, e.g. 2mr as an non-standard spelling for tomorrow. Consequently, in normalization   the standard approach of dealing with spelling variation   so-called non-standard words are mapped to their corresponding standard words. However, there is not always a corresponding standard word. This can be the case for single types (like emoticons in computer-mediated communication) or a complete language, e.g. texts from historical languages that did not develop to a standard variety. The approach presented in this thesis proposal deals with spelling variation in absence of reference to a standard. The task is to detect pairs of types that are variants of the same morphological word. An approach for spelling-variant detection is presented, where pairs of potential spelling variants are generated with Levenshtein distance and subsequently filtered by supervised machine learning. The approach is evaluated on historical Low German texts. {'en': 'We present a cognitive computational model of pronoun resolution that reproduces the human interpretation preferences of the Subject Assignment Strategy and the Parallel Function Strategy. Our model relies on a probabilistic pronoun resolution system trained on corpus data. Factors influencing pronoun resolution are represented as features weighted by their relative importance. {'en': 'Social networks have transformed communication dramatically in recent years through the rise of new platforms and the development of a new language of communication. This landscape requires new forms to describe and predict the behaviour of users in networks. This paper presents an analysis of the frequency distribution of hashtag popularity in Twitter conversations. Our objective is to determine if these frequency distribution follow some well-known frequency distribution that many real-life sets of numerical data satisfy. In particular, we study the similarity of frequency distribution of hashtag popularity with respect to Zipf’s law, an empirical law referring to the phenomenon that many types of data in social sciences can be approximated with a Zipfian distribution. Additionally, we also analyse Benford’s law, is a special case of Zipf’s law, a common pattern about the frequency distribution of leading digits. In order to compute correctly the frequency distribution of hashtag popularity, we need to correct many spelling errors that Twitter’s users introduce. For this purpose we introduce a new filter to correct hashtag mistake based on string distances. Ce paysage nécessite de nouvelles formes pour décrire et prédire le comportement des utilisateurs dans les réseaux. Cet article présente une analyse de la distribution de fréquence de la popularité des hashtags dans les conversations Twitter. Notre objectif est de déterminer si cette distribution de fréquence suit une distribution de fréquence bien connue que de nombreux ensembles réels de données numériques satisfont. En particulier, nous étudions la similitude de la distribution de fréquence de la popularité du hashtag par rapport à la loi de Zipf, une loi empirique faisant référence au phénomène selon lequel de nombreux types de données en sciences sociales peuvent être approchés avec une distribution Zipfian. En outre, nous analysons également la loi de Benford, qui est un cas particulier de la loi de Zipf, un modèle courant concernant la distribution des fréquences des premiers chiffres. {'en': 'Imitation learning is a learning paradigm originally developed to learn robotic controllers from demonstrations by humans, e.g. autonomous flight from pilot demonstrations. Recently, algorithms for structured prediction were proposed under this paradigm and have been applied successfully to a number of tasks including syntactic dependency parsing, information extraction, coreference resolution, dynamic feature selection, semantic parsing and natural language generation. Key advantages are the ability to handle large output search spaces and to learn with non-decomposable loss functions. Our aim in this tutorial is to have a unified presentation of the various imitation algorithms for structure prediction, and show how they can be applied to a variety of NLP tasks. {'en': 'Making decisions in natural language processing problems often involves assigning values to sets of interdependent variables where the expressive dependency structure can influence, or even dictate what assignments are possible. This setting includes a broad range of structured prediction problems such as semantic role labeling, named entity and relation recognition, co-reference resolution, dependency parsing and semantic parsing. The setting is also appropriate for cases that may require making global decisions that involve multiple components, possibly pre-designed or pre-learned, as in event recognition and analysis, summarization, paraphrasing, textual entailment and question answering. In all these cases, it is natural to formulate the decision problem as a constrained optimization problem, with an objective function that is composed of learned models, subject to domain or problem specific constraints. Over the last few years, starting with a couple of papers written by (Roth & Yih, 2004, 2005), dozens of papers have been using the Integer linear programming (ILP) formulation developed there, including several award-winning papers (e.g., (Martins, Smith, & Xing, 2009 ; Koo, Rush, Collins, Jaakkola, & Sontag., 2010 ; Berant, Dagan, & Goldberger, 2011)).This tutorial will present the key ingredients of ILP formulations of natural language processing problems, aiming at guiding readers through the key modeling steps, explaining the learning and inference paradigms and exemplifying these by providing examples from the literature. We will cover a range of topics, from the theoretical foundations of learning and inference with ILP models, to practical modeling guides, to software packages and applications. The goal of this tutorial is to introduce the computational framework to broader ACL community, motivate it as a generic framework for learning and inference in global NLP decision problems, present some of the key theoretical and practical issues involved and survey some of the existing applications of it as a way to promote further development of the framework and additional applications. We will also make connections with some of the hot topics in current NLP research and show how they can be used within the general framework proposed here. The tutorial will thus be useful for many of the senior and junior researchers that have interest in global decision problems in NLP, providing a concise overview of recent perspectives and research net diktuoti, kokie priskyrimai yra įmanomi. Ši parinktis apima įvairias struktūrizuotas prognozavimo problemas, pvz., semantinio vaidmens ženklinimo, pavadinimo subjekto ir santykių pripažinimo, bendros nuorodos pertvarkymo, priklausomybės analizavimo ir semantinio analizavimo. Taip pat tikslinga nustatyti tuos atvejus, kai gali prireikti priimti visuotinius sprendimus, susijusius su keliomis sudėtinėmis dalimis, galbūt iš anksto suprojektuotomis arba iš anksto išmokytomis, pavyzdžiui, atvejų pripažinimu ir analize, santrauka, parafrazėmis, tekstiniu įtraukimu ir atsakymu į klausimus. Visais šiais atvejais yra natūralu, kad sprendimų problem a būtų apibrėžiama kaip ribota optimizacijos problema, turinti objektyvią funkciją, kurią sudaro pasimokyti modeliai, atsižvelgiant į konkrečias sritis ar problem as. Per pastaruosius keletą metų, pradedant keletu dokumentų, kuriuos parašė (Roth & Yih, 2004, 2005), dešimtys dokumentų naudojo ten sukurtą formuluotę „Integer linear programming“ (ILP), įskaitant kelis apdovanojimus laimėjusius dokumentus (pvz., (Martins, Smith, & Xing, 2009; Koo, Rush, Collins, Jaakkola, & Sontag., 2010; Berant, Dagan, & Goldberger, 2011)). Šiame paminėje bus pristatytos pagrindinės TVP formuluotės, skirtos natūralaus kalbų apdorojimo problemoms spręsti, siekiant vadovauti skaitytojams pagrindiniais modeliavimo etapais, paaiškinti mokymosi ir išvadų paradigmas ir\npavyzdys, pateikiant literatūros pavyzdžius. Mes aptarsime įvairias temas, nuo teorinių mokymosi ir išvadų su TVP modeliais pagrindų iki praktinių modeliavimo vadovų, programinės įrangos paketų ir programinių programų. Šio mokymo tikslas – įvesti skaičiavimo sistemą platesnei AKL bendruomenei, motyvuoti ją kaip bendrą mokymosi ir išvadų sistemą pasaulinėse NLP sprendimų problemose, pristatyti kai kuriuos svarbiausius susijusius teorinius ir praktinius klausimus ir išnagrinėti kai kurias esamas jos taikymo sritis kaip būdą toliau plėtoti sistemą ir papildomas taikymo sritis. Ustawienie to obejmuje szeroki zakres problemów przewidywania strukturalnego, takich jak semantyczne oznaczanie roli, rozpoznawanie nazwanych jednostek i relacji, rozwiązywanie współreferencji, parsowanie zależności i parsowanie semantyczne. Ustawienie jest również odpowiednie dla przypadków, które mogą wymagać podejmowania globalnych decyzji, które obejmują wiele komponentów, ewentualnie wstępnie zaprojektowanych lub wcześniej nauczonych, takich jak rozpoznawanie i analiza zdarzeń, podsumowanie, parafrazowanie, zaangażowanie tekstowe i odpowiedzi na pytania. We wszystkich tych przypadkach naturalne jest sformułowanie problemu decyzji jako ograniczonego problemu optymalizacji, z obiektywną funkcją składającą się z nauczonych modeli, podlegających ograniczeniom specyficznym dla domeny lub problemu. W ciągu ostatnich kilku lat, począwszy od kilku artykułów napisanych przez Rotha, Yih, 2004, 2005), dziesiątki artykułów wykorzystują opracowaną tam formułę programowania liniowego Integer (ILP), w tym kilka nagradzanych prac (np. (Martins, Smith, & Xing, 2009; Koo, Rush, Collins, Jaakkola, & Sontag., 2010; Berant, Dagan, & Goldberger, 2011)). Ten poradnik przedstawi kluczowe składniki formuł ILP problemów przetwarzania języka naturalnego, mając na celu poprowadzenie czytelników przez kluczowe etapy modelowania, wyjaśnienie paradygmatów uczenia się i wnioskowania oraz\nprzykładając przykłady z literatury. Obejmiemy szereg tematów, od teoretycznych podstaw uczenia się i wnioskowania z modelami ILP, po praktyczne przewodniki modelowania, po pakiety oprogramowania i aplikacje. {'en': 'In this tutorial, we introduce a computational framework and modeling language (VoxML) for composing multimodal simulations of natural language expressions within a 3D simulation environment (VoxSim). We demonstrate how to construct voxemes, which are visual object representations of linguistic entities. We also show how to compose events and actions over these objects, within a restricted domain of dynamics. This gives us the building blocks to simulate narratives of multiple events or participate in a multimodal dialogue with synthetic agents in the simulation environment. To our knowledge, this is the first time such material has been presented as a tutorial within the CL community. This will be of relevance to students and researchers interested in modeling actionable language, natural language communication with agents and robots, spatial and temporal constraint solving through language, referring expression generation, embodied cognition, as well as minimal model creation. Multimodal simulation of language, particularly motion expressions, brings together a number of existing lines of research from the computational linguistic, semantics, robotics, and formal logic communities, including action and event representation (Di Eugenio, 1991), modeling gestural correlates to NL expressions (Kipp et al., 2007 ; Neff et al., 2008), and action event modeling (Kipper and Palmer, 2000 ; Yang et al., 2015). We combine an approach to event modeling with a scene generation approach akin to those found in work by (Coyne and Sproat, 2001 ; Siskind, 2011 ; Chang et al., 2015). Mapping natural language expressions through a formal model and a dynamic logic interpretation into a visualization of the event described provides an environment for grounding concepts and referring expressions that is interpretable by both a computer and a human user. This opens a variety of avenues for humans to communicate with computerized agents and robots, as in (Matuszek et al., 2013 ; Lauria et al., 2001), (Forbes et al., 2015), and (Deits et al., 2013 ; Walter et al., 2013 ; Tellex et al., 2014). Simulation and automatic visualization of events from natural language descriptions and supplementary modalities, such as gestures, allows humans to use their native capabilities as linguistic and visual interpreters to collaborate on tasks with an artificial agent or to put semantic intuitions to the test in an environment where user and agent share a common context. In previous work (Pustejovsky and Krishnaswamy, 2014 ; Pustejovsky, 2013a), we introduced a method for modeling natural language expressions within a 3D simulation environment built on top of the game development platform Unity (Goldstone, 2009). The goal of that work was to evaluate, through explicit visualizations of linguistic input, the semantic presuppositions inherent in the different lexical choices of an utterance. This work led to two additional lines of research : an explicit encoding for how an object is itself situated relative to its environment ; and an operational characterization of how an object changes its location or how an agent acts on an object over time, e.g., its affordance structure. The former has developed into a semantic notion of situational context, called a habitat (Pustejovsky, 2013a ; McDonald and Pustejovsky, 2014), while the latter is addressed by dynamic interpretations of event structure (Pustejovsky and Moszkowicz, 2011 ; Pustejovsky and Krishnaswamy, 2016b ; Pustejovsky, 2013b).The requirements on building a visual simulation from language include several components. We require a rich type system for lexical items and their composition, as well as a language for modeling the dynamics of events, based on Generative Lexicon (GL). Further, a minimal embedding space (MES) for the simulation must be determined. This is the 3D region within which the state is configured or the event unfolds. Object-based attributes for participants in a situation or event also need to be specified ; e.g., orientation, relative size, default position or pose, etc. The simulation establishes an epistemic condition on the object and event rendering, imposing an implicit point of view (POV). Finally, there must be some sort of agent-dependent embodiment ; this determines the relative scaling of an agent and its event participants and their surroundings, as it engages in the environment. In order to construct a robust simulation from linguistic input, an event and its participants must be embedded within an appropriate minimal embedding space. This must sufficiently enclose the event localization, while optionally including space enough for a frame of reference for the event (the viewers perspective).We first describe the formal multimodal foundations for the modeling language, VoxML, which creates a minimal simulation from the linguistic input interpreted by the multimodal language, DITL. We then describe VoxSim, the compositional modeling and simulation environment, which maps the minimal VoxML model of the linguistic utterance to a simulation in Unity. This knowledge includes specification of object affordances, e.g., what actions are possible or enabled by use an object. VoxML (Pustejovsky and Krishnaswamy, 2016b ; Pustejovsky and Krishnaswamy, 2016a) encodes semantic knowledge of real-world objects represented as 3D models, and of events and attributes related to and enacted over these objects. VoxML goes beyond the limitations of existing 3D visual markup languages by allowing for the encoding of a broad range of semantic knowledge that can be exploited by a simulation platform such as VoxSim. VoxSim (Krishnaswamy and Pustejovsky, 2016a ; Krishnaswamy and Pustejovsky, 2016b) uses object and event semantic knowledge to generate animated scenes in real time without a complex animation interface. It uses the Unity game engine for graphics and I / O processing and takes as input a simple natural language utterance. The parsed utterance is semantically interpreted and transformed into a hybrid dynamic logic representation (DITL), and used to generate a minimal simulation of the event when composed with VoxML Até onde sabemos, esta é a primeira vez que esse material é apresentado como um tutorial dentro da comunidade CL. Isso será de relevância para estudantes e pesquisadores interessados em modelar linguagem acionável, comunicação em linguagem natural com agentes e robôs, resolução de restrições espaciais e temporais através da linguagem, geração de expressão de referência, cognição incorporada, bem como criação de modelo mínimo. A simulação multimodal de linguagem, particularmente expressões de movimento, reúne várias linhas de pesquisa existentes das comunidades de linguística computacional, semântica, robótica e lógica formal, incluindo representação de ação e evento (Di Eugenio, 1991), modelagem gestual correlaciona-se com expressões NL (Kipp et al., 2007; Neff et al., 2008), e modelagem de evento de ação (Kipper e Palmer, 2000; Yang et al., 2015 ). Combinamos uma abordagem de modelagem de eventos com uma abordagem de geração de cenas\nsemelhantes aos encontrados no trabalho de (Coyne e Sproat, 2001; Siskind, 2011; Chang et al., 2015). O mapeamento de expressões de linguagem natural por meio de um modelo formal e uma interpretação lógica dinâmica em uma visualização do evento descrito fornece um ambiente para conceitos básicos e expressões de referência que são interpretáveis por um computador e por um usuário humano. Isso abre uma variedade de caminhos para os humanos se comunicarem com agentes e robôs computadorizados, como em (Matuszek et al., 2013; Lauria et al., 2001), (Forbes et al., 2015) e (Deits et al., 2013; Walter et al., 2013; Tellex et al., 2014). A simulação e a visualização automática de eventos a partir de descrições de linguagem natural e modalidades suplementares, como gestos, permitem que os humanos usem suas capacidades nativas como intérpretes linguísticos e visuais para colaborar em tarefas com um agente artificial ou testar intuições semânticas em um ambiente onde usuário e agente compartilham um contexto comum. ). O objetivo desse trabalho foi avaliar, por meio de visualizações explícitas de input linguístico, os pressupostos semânticos inerentes às diferentes escolhas lexicais de um enunciado. Este trabalho levou a duas linhas adicionais de pesquisa: uma codificação explícita de como um objeto é em si\nsituado em relação ao seu ambiente; e uma caracterização operacional de como um objeto muda sua localização ou como um agente age em um objeto ao longo do tempo, por exemplo, sua estrutura de affordance. O primeiro se desenvolveu em uma noção semântica de contexto situacional, chamado de habitat (Pustejovsky, 2013a; McDonald e Pustejovsky, 2014), enquanto o último é abordado por interpretações dinâmicas da estrutura do evento (Pustejovsky e Moszkowicz, 2011; Pustejovsky e Krishnaswamy, 2016b ; Pustejovsky, 2013b).Os requisitos para construir uma simulação visual a partir da linguagem incluem vários componentes. Exigimos um rico sistema de tipos para itens lexicais e sua composição, bem como uma linguagem para modelar a dinâmica dos eventos, baseada no Generative Lexicon (GL). Além disso, um espaço mínimo de incorporação (MES) para a simulação deve ser determinado. Esta é a região 3D dentro da qual o estado é configurado ou o evento se desenrola. Atributos baseados em objetos para participantes em uma situação ou evento também precisam ser especificados; por exemplo, orientação, tamanho relativo, posição ou pose padrão, etc. A simulação estabelece uma condição epistêmica na renderização do objeto e do evento, impondo um ponto de vista implícito (POV). Finalmente, deve haver algum tipo de incorporação dependente do agente; isso determina o dimensionamento relativo de um agente e seus participantes do evento e seus arredores, conforme ele se envolve no ambiente.\nincorporado dentro de um espaço de incorporação mínimo apropriado. Isso deve incluir suficientemente a localização do evento, enquanto opcionalmente inclui espaço suficiente para um quadro de referência para o evento (perspectiva do espectador). Primeiro descrevemos os fundamentos multimodais formais para a linguagem de modelagem, VoxML, que cria uma simulação mínima a partir do entrada linguística interpretada pela linguagem multimodal, DITL. Em seguida, descrevemos o VoxSim, o ambiente de modelagem e simulação composicional, que mapeia o modelo VoxML mínimo do enunciado linguístico para uma simulação no Unity. Este conhecimento inclui especificação de affordances de objetos, por exemplo, quais ações são possíveis ou habilitadas pelo uso de um objeto. eventos e atributos relacionados e executados sobre esses objetos. Ele usa o mecanismo de jogo Unity para gráficos e processamento de E/S e recebe como entrada um enunciado simples de linguagem natural. Demostramos cómo construir voxemas, que son representaciones visuales de objetos de entidades lingüísticas. También mostramos cómo componer eventos y acciones sobre estos objetos, dentro de un dominio restringido de la dinámica. Esto nos da los componentes básicos para simular narrativas de múltiples eventos o participar en un diálogo multimodal con agentes sintéticos en el entorno de simulación. Hasta donde sabemos, esta es la primera vez que este material se presenta como un tutorial dentro de la comunidad de CL. Será relevante para los estudiantes e investigadores interesados en modelar el lenguaje procesable, la comunicación del lenguaje natural con agentes y robots, la resolución de restricciones espaciales y temporales a través de lenguaje, generación de expresiones de referencia, cognición encarnada, así como creación mínima de modelos. La simulación multimodal del lenguaje, particularmente las expresiones de movimiento, reúne una serie de líneas de investigación existentes de las comunidades lingüística computacional, semántica, robótica y lógica formal, incluyendo la representación de acciones y eventos (Di Eugenio, 1991), el modelado de correlaciones gestuales con las expresiones de NL (Kipp et al., 2007; Neff et al., 2008) y el modelado de eventos de acción (Kipper y Palmer, 2000; Yang et al., 2015). Combinamos un enfoque de modelado de eventos con un enfoque de generación de escenas\nsimilares a los encontrados en el trabajo de (Coyne y Sproat, 2001; Siskind, 2011; Chang et al., 2015). El mapeo de expresiones de lenguaje natural a través de un modelo formal y una interpretación lógica dinámica en una visualización del evento descrito proporciona un entorno para fundamentar conceptos y hacer referencia a expresiones que es interpretable tanto por un ordenador como por un usuario humano. Esto abre una variedad de vías para que los humanos se comuniquen con agentes y robots computarizados, como en (Matuszek et al., 2013; Lauria et al., 2001), (Forbes et al., 2015) y (Deits et al., 2013; Walter et al., 2013; Tellex et al., 2014). La simulación y visualización automática de eventos a partir de descripciones de lenguaje natural y modalidades complementarias, como los gestos, permite a los humanos utilizar sus capacidades nativas como intérpretes lingüísticos y visuales para colaborar en tareas con un agente artificial o poner a prueba las intuiciones semánticas en un entorno en el que el usuario y el agente comparten un contexto común. En trabajos anteriores (Pustejovsky y Krishnaswamy, 2014; Pustejovsky, 2013a), presentamos un método para modelar expresiones de lenguaje natural dentro de un entorno de simulación 3D creado sobre la plataforma de desarrollo de juegos Unity (Goldstone, 2009). El objetivo de ese trabajo era evaluar, a través de visualizaciones explícitas de la información lingüística, los supuestos semánticos inherentes a las diferentes elecciones léxicas de un enunciado. Este trabajo llevó a dos líneas de investigación adicionales: una codificación explícita de cómo es un objeto en sí mismo.\nsituado en relación con su entorno; y una caracterización operativa de cómo un objeto cambia su ubicación o cómo un agente actúa sobre un objeto a lo largo del tiempo, por ejemplo, su estructura de asequibilidad. La primera se ha convertido en una noción semántica de contexto situacional, llamada hábitat (Pustejovsky, 2013a; McDonald y Pustejovsky, 2014), mientras que la segunda se aborda mediante interpretaciones dinámicas de la estructura de los eventos (Pustejovsky y Moszkowicz, 2011; Pustejovsky y Krishnaswamy, 2016b; Pustejovsky, 2013b). los requisitos para crear una simulación visual a partir del lenguaje incluyen varios componentes. Necesitamos un sistema de tipos rico para los elementos léxicos y su composición, así como un lenguaje para modelar la dinámica de los eventos, basado en el Léxico Generativo (GL). Además, se debe determinar un espacio de incrustación mínimo (MES) para la simulación. Esta es la región 3D en la que se configura el estado o se desarrolla el evento. También se deben especificar los atributos basados en objetos para los participantes en una situación o evento; por ejemplo, orientación, tamaño relativo, posición o postura predeterminada, etc. La simulación establece una condición epistémica en la representación del objeto y el evento, imponiendo un punto de vista (PDV) implícito. Finalmente, debe haber algún tipo de encarnación dependiente del agente; esto determina la escala relativa de un agente y sus participantes en el evento y su entorno, a medida que se involucra en el entorno. Para construir una simulación sólida a partir de la información lingüística, un evento y sus participantes deben\nincrustado dentro de un espacio de incrustación mínimo apropiado. Esto debe incluir suficientemente la localización del evento y, opcionalmente, incluir espacio suficiente para un marco de referencia para el evento (la perspectiva del espectador) .Primero describimos los fundamentos multimodales formales del lenguaje de modelado, voXML, que crea una simulación mínima a partir de la entrada lingüística interpretado por el lenguaje multimodal, DITL. A continuación, describimos VoxSim, el entorno de simulación y modelado composicional, que mapea el modelo mínimo de VoXML del enunciado lingüístico en una simulación en Unity. Este conocimiento incluye la especificación de las posibilidades de los objetos, por ejemplo, qué acciones son posibles o se habilitan mediante el uso de un objeto.VOXML (Pustejovsky y Krishnaswamy, 2016b; Pustejovsky y Krishnaswamy, 2016a) codifica el conocimiento semántico de objetos del mundo real representados como modelos 3D, y de eventos y atributos relacionados y promulgado sobre estos objetos. VoXML va más allá de las limitaciones de los lenguajes de marcado visual 3D existentes al permitir la codificación de una amplia gama de conocimientos semánticos que puede aprovechar una plataforma de simulación como Voxsim.Voxsim (Krishnaswamy y Pustejovsky, 2016a; Krishnaswamy y Pustejovsky, 2016b) utiliza objetos y eventos conocimiento semántico para generar escenas animadas en tiempo real sin una interfaz de animación compleja. Utiliza el motor de juego Unity para el procesamiento de gráficos y E/S y toma como entrada un enunciado simple en lenguaje natural. El enunciado analizado es semánticamente\nse interpretan y se transforman en una representación lógica dinámica híbrida (DITL) y se utilizan para generar una simulación mínima del evento cuando se componen con conocimiento de VoXML. Los activos 3D y los objetos nominales y eventos modelados con VoxML se crean con otras herramientas basadas en Unity, y VoxSim utiliza la totalidad de los información para representar una visualización del evento descrito. Los participantes del tutorial aprenderán cómo construir objetos simulables, componer estructuras de eventos dinámicas y simular los eventos que se ejecutan sobre los objetos. El kit de herramientas consiste en compositores de objetos y programas (eventos) y el entorno de ejecución, que permite al usuario manipular directamente los objetos o interactuar con agentes sintéticos en VoxSim. Como resultado de este tutorial, el estudiante adquirirá el siguiente conjunto de habilidades: tomar una geometría de objeto novedosa de una biblioteca y modelarla en VoXML; aplicar comportamientos de biblioteca existentes (acciones o eventos) al nuevo objeto VoXML; modelar atributos de nuevos objetos e introducir atributos novedosos; modelar novedosos comportamientos sobre objetos. Los módulos del tutorial se llevarán a cabo dentro de una imagen de compilación del software. El acceso a las bibliotecas será proporcionado por los instructores. Pustejovsky, 2013a), हमने खेल विकास मंच यूनिटी (गोल्डस्टोन, 2009) के शीर्ष पर निर्मित 3 डी सिमुलेशन वातावरण के भीतर प्राकृतिक भाषा अभिव्यक्तियों को मॉडलिंग के लिए एक विधि पेश की। उस काम का लक्ष्य भाषाई इनपुट के स्पष्ट विज़ुअलाइज़ेशन के माध्यम से मूल्यांकन करना था, एक उच्चारण के विभिन्न लेक्सिकल विकल्पों में निहित शब्दार्थ presuppositions। इस काम ने अनुसंधान की दो अतिरिक्त लाइनों का नेतृत्व किया: एक वस्तु स्वयं कैसे है, इसके लिए एक स्पष्ट एन्कोडिंग\nअपने पर्यावरण के सापेक्ष स्थित; और एक परिचालन लक्षण वर्णन कैसे एक वस्तु अपने स्थान को बदलती है या कैसे एक एजेंट समय के साथ एक वस्तु पर कार्य करता है, उदाहरण के लिए, इसकी affordance संरचना। पूर्व स्थितिजन्य संदर्भ की एक शब्दार्थ धारणा में विकसित हुआ है, जिसे एक निवास स्थान कहा जाता है (पुस्टेजोव्स्की, 2013ए); मैकडॉनल्ड्स और पुस्टेजोव्स्की, 2014), जबकि उत्तरार्द्ध को घटना संरचना की गतिशील व्याख्याओं द्वारा संबोधित किया जाता है (पुस्टेजोव्स्की और मोस्कोविज़, 2011); Pustejovsky और कृष्णास्वामी, 2016b; पुस्टेजोवस्की, 2013 बी)। भाषा से एक दृश्य सिमुलेशन के निर्माण पर आवश्यकताओं में कई घटक शामिल हैं। हमें लेक्सिकल आइटम और उनकी संरचना के लिए एक समृद्ध प्रकार प्रणाली की आवश्यकता होती है, साथ ही साथ घटनाओं की गतिशीलता को मॉडलिंग करने के लिए एक भाषा, जो कि जेनेरेटिव लेक्सिकॉन (जीएल) पर आधारित है। इसके अलावा, सिमुलेशन के लिए एक न्यूनतम एम्बेडिंग स्पेस (एमईएस) निर्धारित किया जाना चाहिए। यह वह 3D क्षेत्र है जिसके भीतर स्थिति कॉन्फ़िगर की गई है या ईवेंट प्रकट होता है। किसी स्थिति या ईवेंट में प्रतिभागियों के लिए ऑब्जेक्ट-आधारित विशेषताओं को भी निर्दिष्ट करने की आवश्यकता है; जैसे, अभिविन्यास, सापेक्ष आकार, डिफ़ॉल्ट स्थिति या मुद्रा, आदि। सिमुलेशन वस्तु और घटना प्रतिपादन पर एक महामारी की स्थिति स्थापित करता है, जो एक अंतर्निहित बिंदु (पीओवी) को लागू करता है। अंत में, किसी प्रकार का एजेंट-निर्भर अवतार होना चाहिए; यह एक एजेंट और उसके ईवेंट प्रतिभागियों और उनके परिवेश के सापेक्ष स्केलिंग को निर्धारित करता है, क्योंकि यह पर्यावरण में संलग्न है। भाषाई इनपुट से एक मजबूत सिमुलेशन का निर्माण करने के लिए, एक घटना और उसके प्रतिभागियों को होना चाहिए\nएक उपयुक्त न्यूनतम एम्बेडिंग स्थान के भीतर एम्बेडेड. यह पर्याप्त रूप से घटना स्थानीयकरण को संलग्न करना चाहिए, जबकि वैकल्पिक रूप से घटना के लिए संदर्भ के एक फ्रेम के लिए पर्याप्त स्थान शामिल है (viewerâ € s परिप्रेक्ष्य)। हम पहले मॉडलिंग भाषा, VoxML के लिए औपचारिक बहुआयामी नींव का वर्णन करते हैं, जो बहुआयामी भाषा, DITL द्वारा व्याख्या किए गए भाषाई इनपुट से एक न्यूनतम सिमुलेशन बनाता है। फिर हम VoxSim, compositional मॉडलिंग और सिमुलेशन वातावरण का वर्णन करते हैं, जो एकता में एक सिमुलेशन के लिए भाषाई उच्चारण के न्यूनतम VoxML मॉडल को मैप करता है। इस ज्ञान में ऑब्जेक्ट affordances का विनिर्देश शामिल है, उदाहरण के लिए, किसी ऑब्जेक्ट का उपयोग करके कौन सी क्रियाएं संभव या सक्षम हैं। वोक्सएमएल (पुस्टेजोव्स्की और कृष्णास्वामी, 2016 बी; Nous montrons comment construire des voxèmes, qui sont des représentations visuelles d'objets d'entités linguistiques. Nous montrons également comment composer des événements et des actions sur ces objets, dans un domaine restreint de dynamique. Cela nous permet de simuler des récits de plusieurs événements ou de participer à un dialogue multimodal avec des agents synthétiques dans l'environnement de simulation. À notre connaissance, c'est la première fois que ce type de matériel est présenté sous forme de tutoriel au sein de la communauté CL. Cela intéressera les étudiants et les chercheurs intéressés par la modélisation d'un langage exploitable, la communication en langage naturel avec des agents et des robots, la résolution de contraintes spatiales et temporelles par langage, génération d'expressions de référence, cognition incarnée, ainsi que création de modèles minimaux.La simulation multimodale du langage, en particulier des expressions de mouvement, rassemble un certain nombre de lignes de recherche existantes issues des communautés linguistique computationnelle, sémantique, robotique et logique formelle, y compris la représentation d'actions et d'événements (Di Eugenio, 1991), la modélisation des corrélats gestuels aux expressions NL (Kipp et al., 2007\xa0; Neff et al., 2008) et la modélisation d'événements d'action (Kipper et Palmer, 2000\xa0; Yang et al., 2015). Nous combinons une approche de modélisation d'événements avec une approche de génération de scène\nsimilaires à ceux trouvés dans les œuvres de (Coyne et Sproat, 2001\xa0; Siskind, 2011\xa0; Chang et al., 2015). La mise en correspondance des expressions du langage naturel au moyen d'un modèle formel et d'une interprétation logique dynamique dans une visualisation de l'événement décrit fournit un environnement pour la mise à la terre des concepts et des expressions de référence qui est interprétable à la fois par un ordinateur et par un utilisateur humain. Cela ouvre diverses voies aux humains pour communiquer avec des agents et des robots informatisés, comme dans (Matuszek et al., 2013\xa0; Lauria et al., 2001), (Forbes et al., 2015) et (Deits et al., 2013\xa0; Walter et al., 2013\xa0; Tellex et al., 2014). La simulation et la visualisation automatique d'événements à partir de descriptions en langage naturel et de modalités supplémentaires, telles que les gestes, permettent aux humains d'utiliser leurs capacités natives en tant qu'interprètes linguistiques et visuels pour collaborer sur des tâches avec un agent artificiel ou pour tester des intuitions sémantiques dans un environnement dans lequel l'utilisateur et l'agent partagent un contexte commun. Dans des travaux précédents (Pustejovsky et Krishnaswamy, 2014\xa0; Pustejovsky, 2013a), nous avons introduit une méthode de modélisation des expressions du langage naturel dans un environnement de simulation 3D construit sur la plateforme de développement de jeux Unity (Goldstone, 2009). L'objectif de ce travail était d'évaluer, au moyen de visualisations explicites d'entrées linguistiques, les présupposés sémantiques inhérents aux différents choix lexicaux d'un énoncé. Ce travail a conduit à deux axes de recherche supplémentaires\xa0: un encodage explicite de la façon dont un objet est lui-même\nsitué par rapport à son environnement\xa0; et une caractérisation opérationnelle de la façon dont un objet change de position ou de la façon dont un agent agit sur un objet au fil du temps, par exemple, sa structure financière. Le premier est devenu une notion sémantique de contexte situationnel, appelée habitat (Pustejovsky, 2013a\xa0; McDonald et Pustejovsky, 2014), tandis que le second est abordé par des interprétations dynamiques de la structure de l'événement (Pustejovsky et Moszkowicz, 2011\xa0; Pustejovsky et Krishnaswamy, 2016b\xa0; Pustejovsky, 2013b). les exigences relatives à la création d'une simulation visuelle à partir du langage comprennent plusieurs éléments. Nous avons besoin d'un système de type riche pour les éléments lexicaux et leur composition, ainsi que d'un langage pour modéliser la dynamique des événements, basé sur Generative Lexicon (GL). En outre, un espace d'intégration minimal (MES) pour la simulation doit être déterminé. Il s'agit de la région 3D dans laquelle l'état est configuré ou l'événement se déroule. Les attributs basés sur l'objet pour les participants à une situation ou à un événement doivent également être spécifiés\xa0; par exemple, l'orientation, la taille relative, la position ou la pose par défaut, etc. La simulation établit une condition épistémique sur le rendu de l'objet et de l'événement, imposant un point de vue implicite (PDV). Enfin, il doit y avoir une sorte de réalisation dépendant de l'agent\xa0; cela détermine l'échelle relative d'un agent et de ses participants à l'événement et de leur environnement, alors qu'il s'engage dans l'environnement.Afin de construire une simulation robuste à partir d'entrées linguistiques, un événement et ses participants doivent être\nintégré dans un espace d'intégration minimal approprié. Cela doit inclure suffisamment la localisation de l'événement, tout en incluant éventuellement suffisamment d'espace pour un cadre de référence pour l'événement (le point de vue du spectateur). Nous décrivons d'abord les bases multimodales formelles du langage de modélisation, VoXML, qui crée une simulation minimale à partir de l'entrée linguistique interprété par le langage multimodal DITL. Nous décrivons ensuite VoxSim, l'environnement de modélisation et de simulation compositionnelle, qui mappe le modèle VoXML minimal de l'énoncé linguistique à une simulation dans Unity. Ces connaissances comprennent la spécification des capacités des objets, par exemple, quelles actions sont possibles ou activées par l'utilisation d'un objet. VOXML (Pustejovsky et Krishnaswamy, 2016b\xa0; Pustejovsky et Krishnaswamy, 2016a) code la connaissance sémantique d'objets du monde réel représentés sous forme de modèles 3D, et d'événements et d'attributs associés et adopté sur ces objets. VoXML va au-delà des limites des langages de balisage visuel 3D existants en permettant l'encodage d'un large éventail de connaissances sémantiques pouvant être exploitées par une plateforme de simulation telle que VoxSim.VoxSim (Krishnaswamy et Pustejovsky, 2016a\xa0; Krishnaswamy et Pustejovsky, 2016b) utilise l'objet et l'événement connaissances sémantiques pour générer des scènes animées en temps réel sans interface d'animation complexe. Il utilise le moteur de jeu Unity pour le traitement des graphiques et des E/S et prend en entrée un simple énoncé en langage naturel. L'énoncé analysé est sémantiquement\ninterprétées et transformées en une représentation logique dynamique hybride (DITL), et utilisées pour générer une simulation minimale de l'événement lorsqu'il est composé avec des connaissances en VoXML. Les ressources 3D et les objets et événements nominaux modélisés par VoxML sont créés avec d'autres outils basés sur Unity, et VoxSim utilise l'intégralité de la composition pour afficher une visualisation de l'événement décrit. Les participants au didacticiel apprendront à créer des objets simulables, à composer des structures d'événements dynamiques et à simuler les événements se déroulant sur les objets. La boîte à outils comprend des compositeurs d'objets et de programmes (événements) et l'environnement d'exécution, qui permet à l'utilisateur de manipuler directement les objets ou d'interagir avec des agents synthétiques dans VoxSim. À la suite de ce tutoriel, l'étudiant acquerra les compétences suivantes\xa0: prendre une nouvelle géométrie d'objet dans une bibliothèque et la modéliser dans VoXML\xa0; appliquer des comportements de bibliothèque existants (actions ou événements) au nouvel objet VoXML\xa0; modéliser les attributs de nouveaux objets et introduire de nouveaux attributs\xa0; modèle roman comportements sur les objets.
